headline: Earnings gather pace; a few loose ends remain

highlights: The portfolio is as diverse as it gets and the very diversity augurs well for its growth in the dynamic Indian energy landscape.

PAT after MI grew 38% YoY to INR 12.5bn, led by Mundra’s return to operations (inoperative in the base quarter), with material contributions from coal JVs, RE generation, Mumbai transmission, and Odisha distribution.
Mundra lifts the growth pack TPWR registered a revenue of INR 199bn (+26% YoY) and an EBITDA of INR 39.2bn (+11% YoY) in Q2.

EBITDA growth was aided by incremental contribution from: 1) standalone operations (~INR 2bn), led by the Mundra plant’s return to operations; 2) RE generation (INR 2.3bn); 3) Odisha discoms (INR 1.3bn); and 4) solar module and cell manufacturing (INR 0.5bn).
valuation: On the downside, RE capacity addition was muted in H1, with ~0.7GW of commissioning against the FY27 target of 2.5GW.
However, management is confident of meeting the full-year target.

watch: Growth firmly intact; a few watch items linger TPWR has a diverse set of growth drivers: 1) RE capacity addition; 2) strong potential in rooftop solar; 3) under-development capacity across transmission, PSP, and hydro power; and 4) a planned 10GW solar wafer and ingot capacity.

However, a few challenges remain, which we continue to monitor: 1) pace of RE commissioning; 2) pending Mundra SPPAs; 3) progress in the Kleros arbitration issue, with a key hearing in the Supreme Court of Singapore scheduled in Jan’27.
